e.etymology: In English a short form of Alfred, Old English for elf counsel. In Scandinavia Alf is a name in its own right, from Old Norse alfr, elf.
namesakes: Alf Landon (Kansas governor and 1936 Republican presidential nominee)

assoc.t: ALF, the furry alien of the 1980s NBC sitcom

e.etymology: The surname French, first given to someone who came from France, used as a given name mostly in the American South.
namesakes: French Stewart (actor on 3rd Rock from the Sun)
e.note: Reads first as the nationality and the language.

e.etymology: In the 19th-century South this was usually a short form of Pinkney, from the surname Pinckney. Today it reads as the color word.

assoc.t: Pink, pop singer of So What and Just Give Me a Reason
PINK, Victoria's Secret's line for young women

e.note: Once a boys' name, it now reads as the color and as the pop singer Pink.

e.etymology: A respelling of Michael, Hebrew Mikha'el, a rhetorical question meaning who is like God? Michael is the archangel who leads the armies of heaven.
An English occupational surname for someone who made or sold gloves, used as a given name in 19th-century America.
A spelling of Birdie, an old pet name from the word bird that also served as a nickname for Bertha and Roberta.
Known through 1950s film star Tab Hunter, born Arthur Kelm, whose stage name was picked by his agent. The name's 1957 peak follows his fame.
namesakes: Tab Hunter (1950s film star and singer of Young Love)
e.note: Also an everyday word (a bar tab, a browser tab) and the name of Coca-Cola's old diet soda.

e.etymology: A short form of Theodosia, from Greek theos, god, and dosis, giving.
Taken up in the 1970s after singer Chaka Khan, born Yvette Stevens, who adopted the name as a teenage activist. Chaka is also an older spelling of Shaka, the Zulu king.
namesakes: Chaka Khan (singer of I'm Every Woman and Ain't Nobody)

assoc.t: Chaka Khan, the Queen of Funk

e.etymology: A spelling of Harold, from Old English here, army, and weald, power or ruler, reinforced by Old Norse Haraldr. Harold II was the English king killed at Hastings in 1066.
A mid-century variant that crosses Lydia with Linda and Lynn.
Usually a spelling of Alvin, from Old English Aelfwine, elf friend. Alvan is also the name of a minor figure in Genesis.
A spelling of Ansel or Ancel, a medieval name from Germanic names that begin with ans, god, such as Anselm.
From Old Norse Gerdr, related to gardr, enclosure; in Norse myth she is the giantess who marries the god Freyr. Gerda is also the girl who rescues Kai in Andersen's The Snow Queen.
A surname used as a given name. Many 19th-century American boys were named Lorenzo Dow, or simply Dow, after the famous traveling Methodist preacher.

assoc.t: the Dow, short for the Dow Jones stock average

e.etymology: A spelling of Bud, an American nickname from buddy, a familiar word for a brother or friend. Budd is also an English surname, as in Melville's Billy Budd.
A spelling of Willard, an English surname from the Germanic name Willihard, from wil, will or desire, and hard, brave or hardy.
A respelling of Helen, Greek Helene, traditionally explained as torch or shining light. In myth Helen of Troy's beauty set off the Trojan War.
A Scottish surname for the officer in charge of a noble household's private rooms, from the Scots form of chamber. It is the Scottish counterpart of the English surname Chambers.
Christopher cut short: the form shows up in late-1980s birth records where the full name ran past a character limit. Christopher is Greek Christophoros, bearer of Christ.
A pet form of Marta, the Spanish form of Martha, Aramaic for lady. Its brief American run followed the Cuban American singer Martika, whose Toy Soldiers reached number one in 1989.
namesakes: Martika (pop singer of the 1989 hit Toy Soldiers)

e.etymology: A short form of Hampton, an English place name and surname that was a favorite given name in the 19th-century South.
Created for the UPN sitcom Moesha, which began in 1996 with the singer Brandy in the title role. The name's peak year in US records is the same year.

assoc.t: Moesha, Brandy's title role in the 1990s UPN sitcom

e.etymology: The word son used as a name, in the same way as Sonny, Bud and Sister, mostly in the South around 1900. The Vietnamese name Son, meaning mountain, is unrelated.
A spelling of Josephine, the French feminine form of Joseph, from Hebrew Yosef, he will add. The spelling follows the pet form Josie.
A spelling of Mamie, a pet form of Mary and Margaret that was at its height in America around 1900, here written under the influence of May.
A surname used as a given name, found mostly in New England in the 19th century.
